days.title: IAM Fundamentals
days.summary: Users, groups, roles and policies; monitoring with CloudTrail and credential reports. Summary, main concepts, flashcards, true/false and pop quizzes.

days.title: EC2 Compute Fundamentals
days.summary: What belongs on EC2, the four instance controls, launching and connecting (SSH, RDP, Session Manager), the instance lifecycle and status checks, and where EC2 sits on the compute spectrum; plus VPC and load-balancing groundwork basics.

days.title: AWS Lambda Fundamentals
days.summary: Serverless: functions, the three invocation modes, memory-driven CPU and the 15-minute ceiling, request + GB-second billing with the permanent free tier, runtimes/zip/container packaging, versions and aliases, execution roles vs resource policies, and Lambda vs EC2 on the compute spectrum.

days.title: S3 and Storage
days.summary: The EC2 storage trio (EBS vs EFS vs instance store), S3 object storage with 11-nines durability and its seven storage classes, hands-on bucket basics (versioning, lifecycle rules, default encryption and deny-all), the EBS deep dive (SSD vs HDD, Multi-Attach, incremental snapshots), plus Storage Gateway, AWS Backup, FSx and Elastic Disaster Recovery, with clickable tier and type drills.

days.title: AWS Networking Fundamentals
days.summary: Amazon VPC from first principles: region-scoped isolation and your own CIDR, the three networking zones, subnets and tiers across AZs, route tables and the internet gateway, NAT gateways, stateful security groups vs stateless NACLs with the ephemeral-ports trap, the five reserved IPs and DHCP option sets, a hands-on two-tier custom VPC build, the inside-out troubleshooting checklist with VPC Reachability Analyzer, and where VPC peering, Transit Gateway and site-to-site VPN fit — with interactive pick-your-fix drills on the classic EC2 port-80-fail cases.

days.title: AWS Database Fundamentals
days.summary: Tables, attributes and tuples, primary and foreign keys; Amazon RDS with its five engines and 12-month free tier plus a hands-on EC2-to-RDS build; the NoSQL trio (key-value, document, graph) and DynamoDB with partition + sort keys, table classes and capacity modes; the RDS-vs-DynamoDB comparison on schema, scaling, locking and cost; Amazon Aurora's up-to-5x performance against proprietary lock-in; migration with AWS DMS and SCT; and the in-memory pair, ElastiCache vs MemoryDB for Redis — with a pick-the-DB service-selection drill.
